segments.text: A coding agent is useful only if you can survive what it does. This is a public Vultr VM. The model comes from Vultr Serverless Inference. Cage gives every run container-scoped blast radius zero, with no host access.

segments.onscreen: write, execute, verify - real exit code and stdout
segments.text: I ask for a chart. The agent writes a Python file through a mediated tool, then executes it inside a fresh container. The run returns a real exit code of zero and real stdout. It prints chart dot png written, plus the size in bytes. The API key stays in the control plane and never enters the sandbox. The timeline records write file, command started, command finished.

segments.onscreen: network none - read-only root - UID 1000 - 512 MB
segments.text: Here is the boundary. Docker shares the host kernel, so kernel escapes are out of scope. The sandbox has no host mount, no network, no IPC sharing, and no API key. The workspace is a 64 megabyte tmpfs, so a runaway writer cannot fill the VM disk. Enforced per task.

segments.onscreen: every tool call has a receipt
segments.text: Second run. I ask the agent to delete the hostname file in etc, through run command. See the tool call, the exit code, and the read only error. The sandbox refuses, and the refusal arrives as a tool result, not a crash. If the model declines, this is the direct drill fallback. The receipt is in the evidence stream.

segments.text: First drill. Delete every file under root, with no preserve flags. The read only root refuses it. The read only canary fails if the rootfs is writable, independent of UID 1000. That control catches a writable root. The cross-task drill checks the peer is alive before asserting isolation. Two sandboxes, one cannot read the other workspace.

segments.onscreen: timeout, PID ceiling, no secrets, no route
segments.text: An infinite loop dies on the inner timeout, exit one twenty four, not memory pressure. A fork bomb hits the process ceiling. Secret and network probes find nothing. Back on the VM, the hostname file is still there, and no sandbox container remains.

segments.onscreen: sealed at completion · Ed25519 · verifier VALID
segments.text: The evidence is sealed at completion. The signature proves this control plane produced the pack, not that the host is honest. The pack holds task, events, signature, public key, and fingerprint. The owner is not in it. The verifier prints VALID. Every tool call has a receipt.
